subject: BrightMesh renewal — pricing & capacity plan
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightmesh.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@brightmesh.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: BrightMesh renewal — request for pricehold & credits

Hi Kimberly,

Our FY27 budget cycle is kicking off and we need to firm the renewal terms with Redwood. Usage has grown ~55% year-over-year and we’re planning to expand the product integration next quarter. Procurement asked me to confirm two things before we loop legal:

- Can Redwood offer a temporary price hold on current per-token rates while we ramp (90 days to 6 months)?
- Is there an onboarding/expansion credit you can apply to the renewal ARR to offset migration costs?

We prefer predictable monthly costs while we validate demand. If there’s a trade (commit increase for deeper protection/credits), we’re open to that — we just need concrete numbers to present to Finance.

Attaching Q3 usage export to ground the ask.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
VP, Cloud Ops | BrightMesh
attachments: usage_report_Q3.csv (csv)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightmesh.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, contracts@brightmesh.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightMesh renewal — request for pricehold & credits

Hi Sara — thanks for the context and the usage file.

We can absolutely design a renewal that balances your need for predictability with Redwood’s capacity planning. High-level proposal for discussion:

1) Staged rate cushion: maintain current published rates for an initial period (proposed 6 weeks to 3 months depending on signed commitment), then stagger a controlled uplift rather than a large step change. Example: 3 months at current rates, followed by 6 months at +4% from the current rate, then normal renewal rates thereafter.

2) Expansion/onboarding credit: one-time credit applied to the renewal invoice. Proposal: $60,000 credit for migration/engineering hours (conditional on a 12-month committed baseline increase).

3) Burst pool & overage guard: include a temporary burst pool (X tokens per month) with a capped overage rate (no more than 3% above baseline effective rate) to avoid surprise bills during ramp.

4) Optional dedicated capacity add-on: if you want guaranteed latency/throughput we can provide a dedicated pool at a predictable blended rate — useful if you plan feature launches.

I attached a short SOW sketch and will loop Ben for the commercial math and Marissa for approval on the credit structure. If you can confirm which of these levers matter most (length of hold vs size of credit vs commit increase), I’ll put a term-sheet together for legal.

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
attachments: BrightMesh_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Quick: trade idea for BrightMesh (internal)

Kimberly — quick thought: if BrightMesh will take a 12-month commit uplift (baseline tokens +20%), we can extend the price hold to 9 months and increase the onboarding credit to $85k. That trade gets Finance comfortable and keeps us covered on utilization.

I’ll run the model and flag any margin pressure, but thought it’s worth having prepped when Sara asks for numbers.

—Ben
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightmesh.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@brightmesh.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightMesh renewal — request for pricehold & credits

Kimberly — really appreciate the quick response and the options. A couple of clarifications from Procurement:

- Would Redwood consider a deeper discount during the protected window? Our ask is current rates for the first 6 months + a temporary -5% net discount applied to consumption invoices for the first 90 days.
- Can the uplift cap be lowered to +4% (instead of +6) after the hold? That will make the business case to Finance.
- On the onboarding credit: would BrightMesh accept $75k if we commit to a 12-month uplift (we’d be willing to increase baseline commit ~18–22%).

Procurement also asked for an indicative term sheet and a PO-ready line item so we can expedite legal. We’d like to have something to review today if possible.

Thanks — looping in contracts@brightmesh.com for visibility.

—Sara
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightmesh.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, contracts@brightmesh.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightMesh renewal — request for pricehold & credits

Sara — thanks, and totally understand Procurement’s desire for concretes. Revised counter (commercial); I’ll get legal to draft a one-page term sheet we can circulate: 

- Protected window: 3 months at current published rates, then 6 months at +4% (effective uplift). We’re willing to make the first 90 days also carry a one-time invoice-level -3% operational discount (net of promos) to help with your ramp cashflow.
- Onboarding/expansion credit: $60,000 applied on renewal execution. If BrightMesh signs for a 20% baseline commit uplift for 12 months (deal_id BM-2026-RNW-34), we can increase the credit to $75,000.
- Burst pool: temporary monthly buffer (configured per SOW) with overage capped at +3% rate and clear telemetry hooks so you can monitor burn.
- SLA protections: additional credit pool triggered if median p95 latency for API calls exceeds 150ms for two consecutive weeks (we can detail exact thresholds in the SOW).

Next steps I propose: Ben will finalize the pricing model and we’ll push a one-page term sheet + a PO-ready invoice line to contracts@brightmesh.com by EOD. Legal redlines can be handled via DocuSign link; please confirm the contact at your side for signature routing.

Linking the HubSpot deal so legal/ops have the reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9999999/BM-2026-RNW-34

If that sounds okay I’ll tag Legal and Finance to prep the doc.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightmesh.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, contracts@brightmesh.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightMesh renewal — request for pricehold & credits

Kimberly — appreciate the flexibility. BrightMesh is comfortable with the revised commercial framework in principle: 3 months current rates + 6 months at +4%, with the conditional $75k credit tied to a 20% commit uplift. Procurement would like the one-page term sheet and a PO-ready invoice line this afternoon so Legal can start redlining.

Please send the DocuSign/term-sheet to contracts@brightmesh.com and cc me; our contracts lead will take it from there.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Lim
VP, Cloud Ops | BrightMesh
